title: 2D Pattern View Controls
content: **List of Contents** Zoom to Selected Zoom Extents All Smart Panning **Objective** **Zoom to Selected** Zoom in to the selected Pattern at your convenience. **Zoom Extents All** Zoom in or out the 2D window to see all Patterns. **Smart Panning** The 2D window is going to pan automatically following the mouse cursor. **Location** **Zoom to Selected** Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ **Focus Zoom** Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ **Zoom to Selected** Click (on Pattern) ▶ **F key on the keyboard** **Zoom Extents All** Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D window) ▶ **Zoom Extents All** **Smart Panning** Main Menu ▶ **Applicable Select/Edit Tool** 3D/ 2D Toolbar ▶ **Applicable Select/Edit Tool** **※ Note:** **Applicable Select/Edit Tool:** Tools used to create pattern/internal shapes, create/edit sewing lines, and create/edit topstitches have smart panning function. **Operation** **Zoom to Selected** 1. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar and select the ![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165245096217) **Transform Pattern** or the ![Edit Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165245101465) **Edit Pattern**. 2. Left click on the pattern to be zoomed in. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶**Focus Zoom** Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ **Zoom to Selected** Left Click (on Pattern) ▶ F key on the keyboard →The 2D window is scaled to the selected pattern and the 2D window can be controlled on the basis of the selected Pattern. **Zoom Extents All** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D window) ▶ **Zoom Extents All** → The 2D window is scaled to show all Patterns in the 2D window. **Smart Panning** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ **Applicable Select/Edit Tool** 3D/ 2D Toolbar ▶ **Applicable Select/Edit Too** l →The 2D Window is going to pan automatically following the mouse cursor. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QYAumSmhqxw Go back to the List of Contents

Follow the indicated guideline: 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Select_Move Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165237010585) **Select/Move Button** ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Buttonhole) Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165205067161) **Select/Move** ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Buttonhole) 2. title: Polygon
content: ### **Objective** Create polygon Patterns in 2D Window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Polygon** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Polygon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165135793049) **Polygon** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Polygon** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Polygon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165135793049) **Polygon** 2. Click on the 2D window to make the start point. 3. Drag the mouse and click as needed to freehand a polygon. 4. Right click while freehanding a polygon. → The Create Polygon window appears. 5. **Length** or **Mirror Creation** options to create polygon more precisely and conveniently. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Length** | Length | Designate the length to be created next. When the **Mirror Creation** option is active, the Length will be applied to the mirrored line as well. **Option** **(ver5.0.0)** | Mirror Creation | The polygon is created symmetrically. The starting point converts to a closed point. Axis | Local | Symmetric lines are created based on the starting point (local). X-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the X-Axis. Y-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the Y-Axis. 6. Click again on the start point to complete the polygon. **※ Note:** * Pressing the keyboard’s Delete key while setting points to create a pattern cancels the points, starting from the most recent one. Furthermore, pressing the Esc/Ctrl+Z key during creation cancels the entire operation. * While making points to create a Pattern, holding down the Ctrl key and setting points turns segment points into Free Curve Points. This creates a polygon Pattern made up of curved lines. * Setting a Segment Point while holding down shift reveals a guideline that can move horizontally, vertically, and diagonally at a 45 degree angle according to the Segment Point.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users through the process of creating precise polygon patterns in a 2D window using various tools and options available in the software.

title: Sew Blocks
content: **List of Contents** Sew Patterns and Block Boxes Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing ### **Objective** Set seamlines between Patterns and Block Boxes. **Location** Modular Mode ▶ **Block Editor** **Operation** **Sew Patterns and Block Boxes** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ **Block Editor** 2. Click on******![Segment Sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165021281305)****Segment sewing** tool or ![Free Sewing.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165036872089) **Free sewing** tool. 3. Set seamlines for Pattern and its relative Block Boxes (Step 2 and 3 do not necessarily need to be in order). 4. Set Pattern outlines (Patterns must be sewn one another i.e. shoulder seams, armholes, side seams) and seamlines between Block Boxes. 5. Repeat the steps above for the remains. **※ Note:** * Block Boxes can only be sewn with **Segment Sewing**. In other words, sewing multiple Block Box segments at once by using **M:N Free Sewing** is not allowed. Therefore if the number of Block Box segments is higher than the number of segments need to be sewn, add segments on the patterns to make the number equal, then sew them 1:1. ex) In case of a basic t-shirt block, there is a point added on the neck segment. Therefore add a point on its pattern, then sew the segments 1:1. * Patterns that are sewn alone (i.e. hems, sleeves or armholes of a sleeveless style) do not need to be sewn to Block Boxes. * Difference in length between the actual Pattern and the Block Boxes has no effect on the simulation. * Rest of the principle is the same as the Simulation Mode. **Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ **Block Editor** 2. 2D Toolbar default presets ![Show Modular Sewing_Show.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165021284889)**Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing** tool. → While the tool is toggled on, it enables to check the seamlines between Patterns and Block Boxes. 3. Deselect ![Show Modular Sewing_Show.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165021284889)**Show modular sewing** / **Show pattern sewing** tool. → Block Boxes to Pattern seamlines disappears but for Patterns to Patterns are appeared. **※ Note:** If seamlines do not appear after setting Pattern and Block Boxes, please confirm ![Show Modular Sewing_Show.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165021284889)**Show modular sewing / Show pattern sewing** toggle status. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for setting seamlines between Patterns and Block Boxes in Modular Mode's Block Editor.

title: 2D Pattern (DXF) Import/Export
content: **List of Contents** Import DXF / Import DXF (Add) Export DXF **Objective** DXF is a standard file format of industrial CAD patterns and stores 2D pattern information. DXF is currently available in Yuka, Gerber, Lectra, StyleCAD, Optitex, PAD System, etc. **DXF-AAMA, DXF-ASTM, Standard DXF(ver 6.2)** files are compatible with most 2D CAD softwares. **※ Note:** The options for exporting DXF files are different for each CAD and the method of organizing the pattern information is different. When importing DXF files on CLO 3D, there may be some problems. In this case, please send the problem file to [CONTACT US](https://www.clo3d.com/en/support/contactus) and we will solve it. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import / Import (Add) / Export ▶ **DXF** ** Operation** **Import DXF / Import DXF (Add)** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. → The file explorer window appears. 2. Select the DXF file and click the **Open**. → Import DXF window appears. 3. Set the details and click **OK**. **Basic** | **Scale** | Select the unit used in the pattern CAD. ---|---|--- **Rotation** | Rotate the entire pattern clockwise/counterclockwise. **Option** **** **** | **Import Pattern Annotation** | Import Pattern Annotation information together. **Auto-Trace as Internal Line** | The entire baseline is traced as an Internal Line. **Swap Cutting Line and Sewing Line** | Check this option when the pattern's Cutting lines and Sewing lines are changed. * The Cutting line and Sewing line may change depending on the export option setting of the pattern CAD. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001304047/03_____________.png) **Include Notches** | When changing the Sewing line and Cutting Line, the notch is moved together. **Auto Distribute** | Closely rearrange the patterns in the DXF file. **Optimize All Curve Points** | Optimizes the number of curve points in the DXF file. **Convert to Seam Allowance (ver 6.1)** | Import CAD seam allowance to CLO seam allowance. **※Note:** The default setting is applied to the type of start, end or edge seam allowance that is not supported by CLO. **Remove Non-Grading Points (ver 6.1)** | Optimize the number of points by deleting Straight/Curve Points that have no grading information. **※Note:** This option is only required for AAMA-format DXF files which is different from CLO's default curve points. **※Note:** Standard DXF files of AutoCAD and Adobe Illustrator can be imported (ver 6.2) **Export DXF** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → The file explorer window appears. 2. Set the file name and save the path and click OK. → The DXF Export window appears. 3. Set the details and click **OK**. **Basic** | **Select Pattern** | Select the size group you want to export from among the grading size groups applied to the file. Only one Size Group can be selected and exported per file. ---|---|--- **DXF Format** | Set the export format. **Size format ** **(ver 7.0)** | Export the grading information by including it in the DXF file or RUL file only. **Scale** | Set the unit of the pattern. **Rotation** | Rotate the entire pattern clockwise/counterclockwise. **Option** | **Export without Grading** | Export the current size only excluding grading information. **Export without Baselines** | Export patterns except for baselines. **Duplicate Notch on Seam Allowance** | Duplicate the notch on the outline of the pattern to the seam allowance. **Swap Cutting Line and Sewing Line** | The type of sewing line and the cutting line defined in CLO and Pattern CAD may be different. In this case, when exporting to DXF, the cutting line and the sewing line are replaced and exported. **Convert Curve Point to Straight Point (AI Only)** | When DXF is imported from AI (Adobe illustrator), the curve information does not come in properly, which may distort part of the pattern. In this case, it can be solved by converting all the curved points of the pattern to straight points. **Optimize All Curve Points** | Easily modify the curve by optimizing the number of curve points added on the line segment. **Export Pattern Bounding Box** **(Single Bounding Box/ Separate Pattern Bounding Box)** | By exporting the pattern with the bounding box, conveniently edit the image when working in photoshop, illustration, etc. ** Export Selected Patterns (ver 6.1) ** | Only the selected pattern is exported not the entire pattern. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive guidance on importing and exporting DXF files in CLO 3D, detailing the necessary steps, available options, and compatibility with various CAD software.

title: Fold 3D Garment
content: **List of Contents** Arrangement and Settings Fold ### **Objective** Fold your 3D garment easily. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Fold 3D Garment** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Fold 3D Garment** **Operation** **Arrangement and Settings** 1. When a 3D garment is draped over an avatar, click the avatar with the Select/Move tool to [Delete](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000434168-Delete-Avatar) it. 2. Click the tool/ menu indicated. → The Fold 3D Garment window appears. 3. To fold a 3D garment efficiently, arrange and set it by clicking each button below. ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410129673369/mceclip0.png) | **Rotate X-Axis** | The tool rotates the 3D garment 90 degrees along the X-axis. When the 3D garment is in the air, it is moved to the center of the ground. ---|---|--- **![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410135395481/mceclip1.png)**| **Flip Horizontally** | Flip the 3D garment horizontally to fold part of the garment above or below the guideline. **※Note:** If a garment is folded in the upward state, it may be unstable due to collision with the ground. It is recommended to fold it in the downward state and then turn it over again. **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410124135065/mceclip2.png)** | **Optimize-Res Garment** | In order to efficiently fold the 3D garment, the Particle Distance and the Add'l Thickness - Collision are applied in batches with optimized values. Optimized values ​​are applied by default, and change as needed. **![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410129686297/mceclip3.png)** | **Set Physical Property for Spreading** | Set the proper physical property for spreading the 3D garment flat on the ground. **![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410135405593/mceclip4.png)**| **Set Physical Property for Folding** | Set the proper physical property for folding the 3D garment easily. **Fold** 1. Click the Fold tool. 2. Click the start point of the line to be folded on the ground or the 3D garment, double click to end it. → The line is created, and the gizmo for rotation appears. 3. Click the gizmo axis (red or yellow-green) in the direction you want to fold to rotate it along the blue circle gizmo. → It rotates in that direction. 4. Simulate the garment. → The garment is simulated in a rotated state. **※Note:** * Click the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410144979481/mceclip1.png)**Fold (Selected)** tool to select and fold only a specific pattern piece. It is helpful when you want to fold a long sleeve one more time. * You can create the horizontal, vertical, and 45-degree guidelines by pressing the Shift on the keyboard while drawing the lines. * To delete the line while drawing, press the ESC on the keyboard. * Click the Fold (Selected) tool to select and fold only a specific pattern piece. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for efficiently folding 3D garments using various tools and settings in the software.

title: Fold Pattern
content: **Objective** Use this function to create a pressing effect by adjusting the angle of Pattern's Internal Line, for instance, pressed lines of formal trousers, fold direction of pleats. ** Location** Pattern Property Editor ▶ Fold ▶ **Fold Angle** ** Operation** 1. Click on an Internal Line with ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005539728/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005492287/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern. ** 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Pattern Property Editor ▶ Fold ▶ **Fold Angle** 3. Adjust the value of **Fold Angle** as desired. **※ Note:** **Fold Strength** | Sets the angle closer as the value increases. The value range is in between 0 to 20. ---|--- **Fold Angle** | Sets the value in the range of 0˚ to 360˚, 180˚ represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0˚, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360˚. **Fold Rendering** | Sets whether the pleats to have soft or sharp edges according to user preference. (Only applicable if Fold Arrangement is used on an Internal line.) ****
content_description: This web page provides a guide for adjusting the Fold Angle of an Internal Line in the Pattern Property Editor to create realistic pressing effects for garments like formal trousers.

title: Use Layer (Drape Additional Garment)
content: ### **Objective** This function allows easier Simulation when setting which layer to get in/outward among overlapped multiple layers. By using this function, taking out inaccurately inwardly simulated patterns such as pockets and buttons, gets easier. In addition, adding additional outerwear on top of garments such as dress and shirts. The default layer value of zero ('0') means the layer function is being off. In that state, the arrangement order of the Patterns gets decided. **Operation** 1. Select a Pattern in the 3D window to set a layer with ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005642368/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** tool. → Pattern property appears in the Property Editor. 2. In the Simulation ▶ **Layer** properties, enter the larer value than the inside pattern for the pattern to be placed on the outside, and enter the smaller value than the outside pattern for the pattern to be placed inside. → The pattern with layer is displayed in color. **※Note:** Right-click on the background of the 3D window and click **Show/Hide Colors****▶ Layer** to hide color. (ver 7.3[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142607041305)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=rDrQIfsgUDAq_FC5&t=1372)) 3. Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005642388/Toolbar_3D_Simulation.png) **Simulation** tool. → The order is applied and simulated according to the set layer values. 4. Once simulating is complete in the desired order, change the layer values for all patterns to 0 for a stable simulation. → The simulated result will remain in order.
content_description: This web page provides a guide for using the layer function in 3D simulation to effectively manage overlapping garment patterns and improve the accuracy of design simulations.

title: Select Mesh & Apply to Selected Meshes
content: **List of Contents** Select Mesh (Brush) / (Lasso) / (Box) Apply to Selected Meshes **Objective** Select some meshes of 3D garment or apply Subdivided, Freeze, Solidify, Solidify to selected meshes. [Watch tutorial video here. ](https://youtu.be/CW6ux_ABzRw) **Location** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ ▶ **Select Mesh (Brush) / (Box)** /**(Lasso)**** ** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900008246903/mceclip0.png)(Click for more than 2 seconds) ▶ **Select Mesh (Brush) / (Box)** /**(Lasso)**** ** **Operation** ******Select Mesh (Brush) / (Box) / (Lasso)** 1. Select the tool/ menu indicated. 2. Click and drag the desired area on a garment. → The area is selected. **※Note:** * Select Mesh (Brush) - Set Strength, Size, and Focal in the Brush window at the top-right corner. * Select Mesh (Lasso) / (Box) - To select meshes additionally, press Shift+Ctrl on the keyboard then click and drag on the garment. To deselect the selected area, press Ctrl and click and drag on the garment. * Select Mesh (Lasso) / (Box) - Double click a Pattern outline/ internal line in either the 3D/ 2D window to select Mesh along the segment. When selecting Mesh on the Pattern, adjacent segment vertices are also selected. **Subdivide / Freeze / Solidify (ver 6.1) / Strengthen (ver 7.1)** 1. Select the tool/ menu indicated. 2. Right-click on the selected meshes and select the menu **Subdivide / Freeze / Solidify (ver 6.1) / Strengthen (ver 7.1).** → Each menu is applied to the meshes and displayed in different colors. 3. Set the properties of the applied options in the property editor. **Subdivide(Mesh)** | **Name** | Name the subdivided mesh area. ---|---|--- **Level** | Set the subdivision level of mesh. The higher the value is, the smaller the mesh is. **Smooth** | Subdivide the area between the subdivided area and the normal area progressively. ** Solidify/Strengthen ** | **Strength** | Set the intensity of Solidify and Strengthen. 4. To apply the desired option, right click the mesh area that each option is applied to. **※Note:** Right-click an empty area in the 3D window and click the Show/ Hide Color menu to hide each color of the mesh areas.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for selecting and manipulating meshes in 3D garment design, including tools for subdivision, freezing, and solidifying selected areas.

title: Bond: How to Add Interlining / Fusible / Reinforcement
content: * To express bonding, select a pattern or internal shape with the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005592407/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** tool. * In the Property Editor, tick on **Bond** under **Bond/Skive**. → The selected component is now being displayed in a semi-transparent orange-brown color. * Under **Physical Property** , find the following options: Preset **Fusible (Common):** Tricot Interfacing, 47gsm **Fusible (Lapel):** Wefted Interfacing, 30gsm **Fusible (Nonwoven):** Fiber Web (pellon brand), 40gsm **Fusible (Nonwoven_Small Parts):** Stronger Fiber Web, 32gsm **Reinforcement (Pocket Bone):** Fiber Web without Fuse, 38-42gsm **Reinforcement (Undercollar):** Hair Cloth (edited), 180gsm Detail By default, these are the same as the fabric's, but can be edited separately if desired. * Upon simulating, the bonded area is now being displayed more stiffly, as if an interlining has been fused onto it.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on using the Transform Pattern tool to create bonded areas in garment design, enhancing the fabric's structure through various fusible and reinforcement options.

title: Cut & Sew
content: **List of Contents** Cut&Sew Use Cut&Sew **Cut&Sew** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bRuPyIoiI3o \- Cut and sew Patterns at once based on the Internal Line. \- The Cut & Sew can be operated with following tools: * Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern** tool * Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Trace** tool ** Use Cut&Sew** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TwjFB1IxryA \- Navigate to and select following tools: * Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern** tool * Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Trace** tool \- Right-click on the Internal Line and select **Cut & Sew** from the pop-up menu. \- The Pattern will cut and sewn based on the Internal Line. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide to using the Cut & Sew feature in pattern design, including instructional videos and step-by-step tool navigation.

title: 2D Seam Allowance
content: **List of Contents** 2D Seam Allowance Create Seam Allowance Select Seam Allowance Delete Seam Allowance **2D Seam Allowance YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kKpMYSii5eU **\- Create, select, and delete seam allowances on Patterns in CLO. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶**Seam Allowance** \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026411067/mceclip0.png) **Seam Allowance** tool from the 2D toolbar. ** Create Seam Allowance YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oht5N_e_J_4 ** \- Click the Pattern outline or Internal Line where seam allowance should be added. 。 \- The seam allowance is created and appears in light-grey. **Select Seam Allowance YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0to2cWSfojA ** \- Click the Pattern outline or Internal Line where the seam allowance is created. \- The seam allowance is selected and its segment is highlighted in yellow. **Delete Seam Allowance YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=19mIXt5frvI ** \- Click the Pattern outline or Internal line where the seam allowance is created. \- The seam allowance is selected and its segment is highlighted in yellow. \- Hit the Delete key on the keyboard to delete the selected seam allowance. \- Or, right click on the Pattern outline or Internal Line where the seam allowance is created. \- Then, select the **Delete** option from the pop-up menu. title: Create an Avatar Fitting Suit (ver 7.3)
content: **Objective** A fitting suit is an invisible component connected to an avatar that enables usage of the [re-drape feature](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034333873-Re-drape-3D-Arrangement-ver-5-1). CLO-native avatars include it by default, while it always has to be added for custom avatars. How to create a fitting suit: YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WRkb4MR0dP0?si=1r9hHwB45kw77gU2&start=1434 **Location** Main Menu▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor**▶ Fitting Suit** ** ****Operation** 1. Load the object to create the fitting suit. 2. Click the tool/menu indicated. → Fitting Suit window appears. 3. [Create the circumference line on](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055394453-Avatar-Measure-ver-6-0-) the avatar's position as the image. → The pattern of the fitting suit is displayed. → The circumference line on both sides are automatically created symmetrically. **※ Note:** You can create each by clicking the Symmetry button off at the top. 4. After creating all circumference line, click the Drape Fitting Suit button. → The fitting suit is draped. **※ Note:** * When you click the Auto-Create Fitting Suit button, the fitting suit is automatically created on your avatar. At this time, if the avatar is not created properly, we recommend creating it manually. * You can delete it by selecting the circumference line you want to delete from the avatar or by selecting the item in the fitting suit window and clicking the delete button. * You can return to the initial state by clicking the reset button.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to creating a fitting suit for avatars in CLO, enabling the use of the re-drape feature for enhanced customization.

title: Walk Pattern
content: **Objective** Compare the length of two segments of different Patterns in real-time by temporarily aligning each other. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K9VQY4VAi7g ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Walk Pattern**** **2D Toolbar ▶****![pattern_walking.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36790602293657)**Walk Pattern** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Walk Pattern**** **2D Toolbar ▶****![pattern_walking.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36790602293657)**Walk Pattern**** ** 2. Click on a point or a part of a pattern outline. → The point or the part of a pattern outline is selected and an arrow appears in between the selected point and the mouse cursor. 3. Click on a point or a part of a pattern outline of the pattern to be compared with the one selected at step 2. → The preview of the pattern selected at step 2 moves next to the clicked position. 4. Move the mouse cursor along the pattern outline: → The preview moves along the pattern outline. → The length of the segment appears at the center of the yellow guideline. 5. Hit enter on the keyboard to complete pattern-walking. ** ※Note: ** * During pattern length comparison, right-click to set options for adding notches to **Walked/Stationary Pattern** , **Move Walked Pattern to Intersection** and **Flip Horizontally (ver 6.1)**.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for real-time comparison of segment lengths between different patterns using the Walk Pattern feature in CLO 3D.

title: Auto Fitting
content: ### **Objective** Automatically fit patterns to an avatar's size. **※ Note:** Auto Fitting is supported with CLO avatars and any custom avatars that have a [Fitting Suit](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/24451580024601-Create-the-Avatar-Fitting-Suit-ver-7-3) applied. **※ Note:** This feature was previously called Auto Grading (v 7.2 and below). **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Auto Fitting** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Auto_Grading.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360043525114) **Auto Fitting** ### **Operation** 1. Adjust the [avatar size](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360013257553-%EC%95%84%EB%B0%94%ED%83%80-%EC%82%AC%EC%9D%B4%EC%A6%88-%EC%A1%B0%EC%A0%88-ver5-0-0-%EC%9D%B4%EC%83%81-) and drape 3D garments on the avatar. **※ Note:** Please set Particle Distance as 20mm for the most optimized result. 2. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Auto Fitting** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Auto_Grading.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360043525114) **Auto Fitting ** → The Auto Fitting window appears. 3. Adjust the below options as needed and click OK. **Maintain Pattern Curvature(%)** | Configure the extent of modification of pattern curvature. Higher the value is, less affected curvature while resizing the patterns. On the other hand, lower the value is, both curvature and size of the patterns are modified. ---|--- **Maintain Graphic Size** | ON | Graphics maintain their size. OFF | The size of graphics are adjusted based on the size changes of the patterns. → The 3D garment is auto-fitted and [draped](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034333873-%EC%9E%90%EB%8F%99-%EB%93%9C%EB%A0%88%EC%9D%B4%ED%95%91) on the avatar.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to automatically fit 2D patterns to an avatar's size using the Auto Fitting feature in CLO software.

title: Garment Fit Maps
content: **Objective** Utilize the four Garment Fit Maps in the 3D window to check the fit of garments. ** Location** 3D Window ▶ hover the mouse over the 7th icon ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window ▶ hover the mouse over the 7th icon → Four Garment Fit Maps appear. 2. Refer to the table below and select the desired view icon. **Icon** | **Description** ---|--- Stress Map | Force along the fabric grain per unit area of the fabric that causes garment deformation; appears in a range of colors and numbers. The Stress Map appears in a total eight colors: Red indicates the strongest stress (100kPa) while blue indicates zero distortion (0.00kPa). Other numbers in between are expressed as a gradation of two colors. Strain Map | Garment's stretch rate due to external force; appears in percentage. The Strain Map appears in a total of eight colors: Red indicates 120% of stretch rate while blue indicates 100% (no stretch). Numbers in between are expressed as a gradation of two colors. Fit Map | The Fit Map shows tightness of the garment. **Can't Wear** appears in red indicating a non-wearable area. **Very Tight** appears in orange indicating a very tight area. **Tight** appears in yellow indicating a slightly tight area. Pressure Map | External pressure exerted by garments onto avatars. → Based on the selected icon, the Stress Map, Strain Map, Fit Map, or Pressure Map appear on the garment.
content_description: Explore the four Garment Fit Maps in the 3D window to assess garment fit and deformation visually.

title: Camera Motion
content: ### **List of Contents** **Add KeyFrame** **Move/Delete KeyFrame** **Show/Hide Camera Path** **Save/Open Camera Motion File** ### ### **Objective** Create more dynamic animations with various camera positions and angles. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CwB8_ad328M?si=gxacEI3f9L7l20W2&start=1026 ### **Location** [Animation Mode ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000523667-Animation) ### **Operation** #### **Add KeyFrame** 1. Click where you want to add a keyframe on the timeline, or move the playhead to the desired position. 2. Control the [3D Window](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000468748--View-Control-Zoom-In-Out-Rotation) view and click the Add/Replace Camera Keyframe button. → Keyframes are added based on the state of the controlled view. 3. If you want to move and rotate the camera yourself, click Camera ViewFinder button. → The camera object is displayed in the 3D window, and the Camera Preview window (ViewFinder) appears. **※ Note:** The screen size of the camera preview window is applied according to the size set in the [render image properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014785207-Edit-V-Ray-Image-Video-Properties). The window screen size can be adjusted by clicking and dragging the bottom right corner. 4. Click the camera or the point displayed on the target of the camera in the 3D window. → [Gizmo](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000513928-Move-Rotate-Pattern-with-Gizmo-) appears. 5. Click and drag each axis of the gizmo to move it directly, or enter each value directly in the property editor. → A keyframe for that camera is added to the timeline at the position of the playhead. **※ Note:** Click the group button at the top right of the gizmo to simultaneously move and rotate the camera and its position relative to its target. 6. After selecting the added keyframe, then adjust the view. → The camera view of the keyframe is changed. #### **Move/Delete KeyFrame** 1. Click and drag the added keyframe to the desired position. → The keyframe is moved to that position. 2. Or right-click on the keyframe you want to delete. → The keyframe is deleted. #### **Show/Hide Camera Path** 1. Click the Show Camera Path button. → Shows or hides paths between camera positions for each keyframe. #### **Save/Open Camera Motion File** 1. Click Main Menu » Save As/Open » Camera Motion. → A camera motion file (CAK) is saved or opened.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for enhancing animation dynamics through the use of keyframes and camera controls.

title: Register Custom OBJ as Buttons
content: **List of Contents** Register Button Add Button **Register Button YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O-WOh22YYaM **\- Register custom OBJ files as buttons as needed. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select Materials ▶ Button ▶**Register Button. ** \- Or, select a desired button style from the Object Browser ▶ **Button Tab**. Then, navigate to the Property Editor to find the **Register Button** button next to the Shape toggle down menu. ** Add Button YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PbwMLb4qeHk ** \- Follow the indicated path above and select the **Register Button** button. \- The **Register Button** window appears. \- Name the button. \- Select the Search button next to the **OBJ** menu to choose a custom OBJ file. \- Select the **+** button next to the Thumbnail menu to load a custom image to be the button’s thumbnail. \- Select **OK** to complete the registration. \- The registered button appears in the following path: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Button (Select a Style) ▶ Property Editor ▶ **Shape.** \- The registered button is saved into the CLO library under Hardware and Trims ▶ Button & Buttonhole ▶ Button. title: Register Hair/Shoes
content: OBJ production Register **Objective** Register the Avatar's Hair/Shoes as an accessory file(ZACS). **Location** Main menu**▶** Avatar**▶ Register Hair/Shoes** ** Operation** **OBJ production** When making OBJ in other 3D programs(Maya, 3ds Max, etc.), please follow the requirements below. 1. Set the work environment of the 3D program. (Axis: Y-Up, Unit: Millimeter) 2. Create a hair/shoes OBJ according to the avatar file. **Avatar** | Prepare an avatar suitable for the hair/shoes to be registered. CLO's default avatar or user avatar can be used. ---|--- **Mesh** | For the sharp angular expression, add an edge to the mesh to be reliably simulated in the CLO. **Dummy** **Mesh** | For complex areas (shoelaces, heels, etc.) where the faces come into contact, wrap in a transparent and flat dummy mesh. Make the spacing between dummy meshes smaller and more consistent than shoe meshes. ![afceb30d-87c7-4216-9e12-09d416d724ce.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360101299113) **Meah** **Name** | **Hair** | hair **Shoes** | ![5f603b9a-10ee-4566-99cc-a65d8cfc67e2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360099067434)(shoes_r, shoes_l) **Materials** | Apply separately various materials(leather, metal, plastic, etc.) Even if the heel is the same material, it must be applied separately and the order must be at the bottom. ![9f3cb925-9f44-46fd-9c50-28b412f6a1ec.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/1500000189402)![25966d9e-df58-4556-9750-145229a14af1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360099067994) 3. Set the transform properties. (Translate/ Rotation: All axes 0, Scale: All axes 1) ![512e752f-6fcf-4ab8-a1fa-2af6e68d2d83.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/1500000202121) 4. Export to FBX file. **Register** 1. Open the avatar file for the hair/shoes to be registered. **※ Note:** It is recommended to open additionally the hair/shoes file(FBX) to be registered and check that the position with the avatar is correct. 2. Select the tool/menu indicated. → The Hair/Shoes registration window appears. 3. After setting the following options, click the Create button. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Hair/Shoes** | Select the type of hair, shoes and glasses & earrings(ver 7.1). **File Path (FBX)** | Select the path of the hair and shoe files to be registered. **Thumbnail** | Add a thumbnail image to be displayed in the library window. → The save file window appears. 4. Set the file name and path. → It is saved as a hair/shoes file(ZACS). **Trouble-Shooting** 1. Make sure the mesh layer noted below has the correct nomenclature in Blender. The other names do not matter. Otherwise, you may encounter an error message that the name is wrong. ![image.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/41144920579225)
content_description: This webpage provides detailed instructions for registering hair and shoes as accessory files (ZACS) for avatars in CLO, including necessary 3D modeling specifications and registration steps.

title: Show Pattern Annotations and Symbols
content: **List of Contents** Show Pattern Annotations and Symbols Importing a DXF File With Pattern Annotations **Show Pattern Annotations and Symbols** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/43618379483289) To show or hide both pattern annotations and symbols, in the 2D window's vertical toggle menu, hover above the **Information Display** icon and select **Show Annotations**. title: Add & Apply Fabric Style
content: **List of Contents** Add a Fabric Apply a Fabric Group Setting (ver 7.1) How to Delete a Fabric **Objective** Add fabric style and apply it to the garment. ![2025-10-13 16_46_49-CLO Network OnlineAuth.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51497099027097) **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab **Operation ** **How to Add a Fabric** Select the Fabric tab in the Object Browser * **The Add Button** * Click **Add** at the top right. * A Default Fabric will be added. * **The Fabric Library** * Open the CLO Fabric Library * Double Click the Fabric (.zfab) or click & drag the fabric and drop into the Fabric Tab. * A Default Fabric will be added. **How to Assign a Fabric** Select the Fabric tab in the Object Browser * **Assign to Selected Patterns Button** * Select a pattern(s) then click the **Assign** button to the right of the Fabric. → The Fabric is applied to the pattern. * **Drag and Drop to Assign** * Drag the fabric directly onto the pattern piece in either the 2D or 3D window to apply it. → The Fabric is applied to the pattern. **Group Setting (ver 7.1)** * To set Fabric Groups, Click the **Create New Folder** button at the top left of the Fabric tab. → A new folder group is created. * Click the **Add Fabric** or **Open Fabric Files** buttons on the right side of the group to load the Fabric file. → A Fabric style is added or opened to the group. * Click the **Edit Folder Name** button on the left of the group to edit the name. Or drag the Fabric style to another group to change the group. **How to Delete a Fabric** A fabric in the Object Browser can only be deleted if not assigned to any pattern pieces in your 2D/3D workspace * **Delete Icon** * Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51497099033497) **Delete** icon next to the Fabric Item. → The Fabric is deleted from the Object Browser * **Delete Option from Right Click Drop Down Menu** * Right Click on the Fabric to be deleted and select Delete from the Drop Down Menu → The Fabric is deleted from the Object Browser * **Delete Key on Keyboard** * Select the fabric to be deleted and press the **Delete** key on the keyboard → The Fabric is deleted from the Object Browser Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for adding, applying, and managing fabric styles within CLO 3D, including step-by-step instructions for fabric operations and group settings.
